title: Python basics
description: Sample quiz: types, truthiness, immutability, indexing, and the main guard.

questions.question: What does `print(type(3 / 2))` display in Python 3?
questions.justification: The `/` operator always performs true division and returns a float in Python 3, so `3 / 2` is `1.5`. Use `//` for floor division, which returns an int when both operands are ints.

questions.question: What does `bool([])` evaluate to?
questions.justification: Empty containers (lists, tuples, dicts, sets, strings) are falsy. A non-empty list is truthy, even if it only contains falsy values such as `[0]`.

questions.question: Which of these built-in types are immutable? (Select all that apply)
questions.justification: Tuples, strings, and frozensets cannot be changed after creation. Lists and dicts are mutable. Immutability matters because only hashable (in practice, immutable) objects can be dict keys or set members.

questions.question: What does `[1, 2, 3][-1]` return?
questions.justification: A negative index counts from the end of the sequence, so `-1` is the last element. An IndexError would occur only if the magnitude exceeded the length, such as `-4` here.

questions.question: When does the body of `if __name__ == '__main__':` run?

choices.A: Every time the module is imported
choices.B: Only when the file is run directly as a script
choices.C: Never, because it is a reserved block
choices.D: Only in an interactive interpreter session

questions.justification: When a file runs directly, Python sets `__name__` to `'__main__'`. When another module imports it, `__name__` is the module's name instead, so the guarded code does not run.
